title: Per-key delta reconciliation breaks under async replay and route-weight adjustments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Users are observing transient over-allow windows for specific API keys after edge replay/failover events. The policy engine is producing incorrect per-key deltas when async_replay merges arrive concurrently with route-weight adjustments. This causes brief but measurable free allowance or double-billing in rare failover/replay scenarios for routes that have non-uniform weightings.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create an org with a per-key quota and a weighted per-route policy (route A weight=0.7, route B weight=0.3).
2) Generate a burst of streaming requests to route A that trigger KV cache population and high batching. Ensure requests are pinned to shard-12.
3) Simulate a shard restart and enable async_replay path so in-flight completions are re-emitted to another shard.
4) While replay traffic arrives, perform a route config update that adjusts weights (A -> 0.6, B -> 0.4) and trigger a compact-policy-sync.

5) Observe per-key allowance counters and billing events in metrics: some keys show net negative debit for a short window (indicating an allow after debit reversal) or duplicated debit events in logs.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial report from support; customer reported occasional ~30s periods where token usage did not decrement for some keys after region failover.

2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging with controlled shard restart; captured request traces and meter events. Replay path merges replayed usage into aggregator without applying the same rounding/weighting order as primary path.

2026-03-12: Found that route-weight normalization was applied before shard-merge adjustments on the primary path but after delta aggregation on replay path, producing a momentary mismatch for fractional-credit math.
2026-03-13: Benchmarked 10k simulated replays; 0.9% exhibited net delta drift > 1 token due to rounding + race ordering at the aggregator's fold step.

2026-03-13: Confirmed logs where replayed-event tombstones and aggregator-compaction race allowed previously-applied debits to be tombstoned but replayed events re-applied without idempotency checks when route metadata changed.
2026-03-14: Reviewed with runtime team; agreed root cause likely ordering + missing idempotency window in replay merge code path.
root_cause: Asynchronous replay merge path applies route weight adjustments and rounding at a different point in the aggregation pipeline compared to the primary fast-path. When a route config change coincides with in-flight replay merge, the aggregator can apply deltas against stale normalization state and re-emit debits without salted idempotency checks, causing brief allowance windows or duplicate debits.
mitigation: Hotfix: Disable async_replay merge path for orgs with recent route-weight updates for 60s as a protective measure until fix is rolled out.
Backfill: Run a reconciliation job to detect affected keys and re-emit compensating debits for double-allow cases (low-volume per-customer), with audit logging enabled.
Monitoring: Add a realtime alert for per-key debit drift > 1 token over a 1m sliding window and a dashboard showing 'replay-merge' events correlated with 'policy-update' events.
proposed_fix: Unify weighting and rounding semantics across fast-path and replay merge by moving normalization to the aggregator's canonical fold step and introduce a 2s idempotency window keyed by (event_id, key, route_epoch). Add unit tests that simulate concurrent policy-update + replay merge, and an integration test using staged shard restarts.
rollout_plan: 2) Deploy to canary (10% of orgs) and monitor debit-drift alert for 24 hours.
3) If stable, increase to 50% for 6 hours and run reconciliation job in parallel to detect previously impacted keys.
4) Full rollout and flip feature flag off after 48h clean window.
5) Post-mortem and update runbooks for shard failovers to include protective config toggle.
tests: Unit: Add deterministic float rounding tests for per-route weighting applied at aggregator fold with synthetic fractional tokens.
Integration: Simulate real shard restart and concurrent policy update to assert no net delta drift across 10k simulated keys.
E2E: Smoke tests ensuring billing pipeline idempotency under replay with route updates.
